content.title: What is the Spring Equinox? - Answered - Twinkl Teaching Wiki
content.text: Are you wondering what is the spring equinox all about? Wonder no more! Read through this handy guide to teach you everything you need to know about the spring equinox with some suggested resources to help you teach your pupils about it.What is the spring equinox? The spring equinox is a pretty exciting point of the year because it is the first day of spring, so it marks the official beginning of the spring and the end of the winter. The spring equinox usually falls around the 21st March each year. It is an event that indicates the start of spring, so we can look forward to the warm months ahead. The spring equinox is also sometimes referred to as the vernal equinox or the March equinox. In 2021, the spring equinox will fall on Saturday 20th March (at 9:37 am). If you’re looking for more information to help teach your children about the spring equinox, check out our What is the Spring Equinox Fact File. What is an equinox? The word equinox is Latin and means ‘equality of night and day.’ So, the equinox comes at a specific moment in time when the sun is exactly above the equator. In fact, the sun is located exactly above the equator twice a year, so there are two equinoxes each year. The other equinox marks the beginning of autumn, and takes place around the 22nd September each year. This equinox happens when the sun crosses the celestial equator going south. For people that live in the Southern Hemisphere, September marks the beginning of their springtime. Many people think that an equinox lasts an entire day, however, this is not true. It is only a certain point of the day that is actually classed as the equinox as that is the point where the sun is directly above the equator. When the spring equinox and autumn equinox take place, everyone receives 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night. Generally speaking, this is true. However, technically, people tend to get around eight minutes more of daytime than night-time. What is an equilux? You may have heard the term ‘equilux’ when talking about the autumn or spring equinox. An equilux is a day in which the durations of light and darkness are exactly equal. Equilux means equal light. This day usually occurs a few days before the spring equinox (in the Northern Hemisphere) and a few days after the autumn equinox (in the Northern Hemisphere). Celebrating the spring equinox Many people and cultures around the world celebrate the spring equinox. For example, the spring equinox marks the start of a new year for people who live in Iran, Afghanistan, the Kurdish regions of Iraq, Turkey, Syria, and throughout Central Asia. This is in accordance with the Persian calendar, and this celebration is known as Nowruz. This has been celebrated for over 3,000 years. People celebrate Nowruz for two weeks, and often spend it seeing relatives, eating traditional food and travelling. Lots of people also believe that the spring equinox is Earth Day (although many people celebrate it in April). This day, for many people, is a day to come together and celebrate the one thing we all have in common: living on Earth. Many people also prepare for Easter on the spring equinox. The spring equinox actually plays an important role in calculating the dates for when to celebrate Christian Easter (as well as Jewish Passover). Did you know? Easter Sunday typically falls on the first Sunday after the first full moon occurring on or after the spring equinox. Find more about the shared themes between Easter and the Spring Equinox in this handy PowerPoint. What happens after the spring equinox? In the Northern Hemisphere, the spring equinox marks the beginning of springtime, and therefore the lead-up to the warmer, summer months. The spring equinox means there will be earlier sunrises, later sunsets, and less wind and rain. This means the days will be longer, sunnier, and warmer. Springtime is also where many plants and flowers start to bloom and grow, and many animals (like sheep) have babies in springtime, because the mild temperatures give them the best chance of surviving.
